evals.prompt: When collecting S3 resiliency data across our buckets, `s3:GetBucketVersioning` returned HTTP 200 `{}` (no `Status` key), `s3:GetBucketLogging` returned HTTP 200 `{}` (no `LoggingEnabled` key), `s3:GetBucketReplication` raised `ReplicationConfigurationNotFoundError`, and `s3:GetObjectLockConfiguration` returned HTTP 403 `AccessDenied`. evals.expected_output: Activates storage-s3-resiliency-expertise and explains: empty HTTP 200 bodies on `GetBucketVersioning` and `GetBucketLogging` do NOT raise `NoSuch*` errors and must be mapped to **`NotConfigured`** (never `OK`!), `ReplicationConfigurationNotFoundError` maps to **`NotConfigured`**, and HTTP 403 `AccessDenied` on `GetObjectLockConfiguration` maps to **`AccessDenied`** (`Unable to verify (access denied)` + pre-flight Permissions Notice + caps Resiliency Rating at `Medium` if continued, never conflated with `NotConfigured`!). Also explains Phase 3 conditional check: when `logging` is `NotConfigured`, inspect `cloudtrail:DescribeTrails` + `GetEventSelectors` for S3 data events covering the bucket (and `s3control:GetPublicAccessBlock` when bucket-level BPA is `NotConfigured`).
expectations: Activates the storage-s3-resiliency-expertise skill

Specifies the Phase 3 conditional fallback when server access logging is `NotConfigured`: checking `cloudtrail:DescribeTrails` and `GetEventSelectors` to see if CloudTrail S3 data events cover the bucket

evals.prompt: Evaluate two S3 replication setups under the S3 resiliency finding logic: (1) Bucket A replicates within the same region (`ap-south-1` -> `ap-south-1`) with `DeleteMarkerReplication: Enabled`, and (2) Bucket B replicates to `arn:aws:s3:::dr-vault-eu-west-1` owned by our isolated DR AWS account, so calling `HeadBucket` on `dr-vault-eu-west-1` from the workload account returns `403 Forbidden`. How does the resiliency review score both cases?
evals.expected_output: Activates storage-s3-resiliency-expertise and explains: (1) same-region replication (`SRR`) does not protect against a regional outage (`⚠️ Same-region only` vs `✅ Cross-region`), AND enabling `DeleteMarkerReplication: Enabled` replicates accidental or malicious mass `DeleteObject` delete markers to the replica (risking synchronized deletion unless paired with Object Lock!), and (2) a `403` on `HeadBucket` for a cross-account destination bucket is expected (`destination_lookup: "lookup_failed"`) and must **not** be treated as a `ToolingFailure` or `AccessDenied` gap on the source bucket.
expectations: Activates the storage-s3-resiliency-expertise skill

Flags same-region replication as lacking regional disaster recovery protection compared to Cross-Region Replication (CRR), and warns of the delete-marker replication risk (`DeleteMarkerReplication: Enabled` propagating bulk deletes to the replica unless mitigated by Object Lock / versioning controls)

Explains that a `403` on `HeadBucket` for a cross-account replication destination bucket is expected (`destination_lookup: "lookup_failed"`) and is **not** scored as a source-bucket `AccessDenied` or `ToolingFailure`

evals.prompt: An older production S3 bucket has `OwnershipControls: BucketOwnerPreferred` (not `BucketOwnerEnforced`), legacy cross-account writer ACL grants in `GetBucketAcl`, and static website hosting enabled (`GetBucketWebsite` returns `IndexDocument: index.html`). expectations: Activates the storage-s3-resiliency-expertise skill

Contrasts `BucketOwnerPreferred` against `BucketOwnerEnforced` (which disables ACLs entirely and ensures uniform bucket-owner ownership) and outlines migrating active cross-account ACL permissions into the Bucket Policy before enforcing `BucketOwnerEnforced`

Flags S3 Static Website Hosting because S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS/TLS and require public read access, recommending Amazon CloudFront with Origin Access Control (OAC) and Block Public Access enabled
